subject: Clarification: US privacy annex — telemetry routing and emergency subprocessor onboarding
messages:
From: Laura Fields <privacylegal@healthco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <procure@healthco.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: US privacy annex — telemetry routing & emergency subprocessor onboarding

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the DPA draft; we reviewed the US-state privacy annex and have two immediate concerns before we can push this to procurement:

1) Telemetry routing / scope: the annex currently describes "telemetry" generically. HealthCo needs the annex to explicitly state that telemetry related to customer PII (IP addresses, user ids, device identifiers) will be treated as covered personal information and only routed to vendors designated in Appendix A (onshore or US-based).

2) Emergency subprocessor onboarding: we learned that Redwood may onboard short-term logging/metrics vendors (for spikes/bursting). We need a short-notice onboarding flow: a) max 72-hour notice to HealthCo privacy team, b) emergency subprocessor must be constrained to aggregated non-identifying telemetry unless explicit consent is obtained, and c) HealthCo must be allowed to request immediate mitigation or onshore fallback.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to: explicit telemetry scoping in the annex, a 72-hour notification SLA, and either an onshore fallback for covered telemetry or a technical mitigation (pseudonymization/encryption) during the emergency window?

Please loop in your security and contracts folks and send over any redlines or evidence (SOC2, dataflow). Procurement will need an exec summary and any vendor attestations.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is looking to finalize by end of quarter.

Best,

Laura Fields
Privacy Counsel, HealthCo
privacylegal@healthco.com

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Monica and Rafael to confirm contractual language and security controls. Quick summary from my side:

- We can add explicit telemetry scoping language that distinguishes PII-bearing telemetry vs aggregated metrics.
- For emergency subprocessors, our playbook supports short-term vendor onboarding but we typically rely on contractual commitments plus post-onboard attestations.
- Onshore fallback is available via our Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers can get pseudonymization and tighter retention windows as mitigations.

Next steps I propose: Monica will suggest concrete redline language for the annex (including a 72-hour notice clause and onshore fallback alternatives). Rafael will attach the SOC2 and a short dataflow diagram showing where telemetry is stored and how we can limit exports.

I attached a short DPA excerpt with proposed phrasing for the telemetry clause. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to run through procurement's checklist.

Hi Laura / team — I reviewed the draft and Dylan's summary. Proposed contract-level bullets below (redline suggestions attached):

- Define "Covered Telemetry" as telemetry elements that can reasonably identify an individual (examples: user_id, device_id, IP address, persistent cookie IDs).
- Redwood will process Covered Telemetry only for the purposes of providing inference observability and platform health. Any export to subprocessors must be limited to "Operational Support" and documented in Appendix A.
- Emergency Subprocessor Onboarding: Redwood may engage a temporary subprocessor for incident response or burst capacity provided that: (i) Redwood notifies the customer within 72 hours of engagement; (ii) the subprocessor is bound by equivalent contractual obligations; (iii) Covered Telemetry must be pseudonymized prior to export except where pseudonymization would prevent necessary incident response, in which case the customer may require an onshore fallback or immediate suspension.
- Retention: Covered Telemetry retention for hosted plans shall not exceed 30 days by default; longer retention requires explicit customer opt-in and documented business justification.

We can also provide a tracked redline (see attached redline_dpa_excerpt.pdf) and a two-paragraph exec summary for procurement.

If HealthCo needs KMS customer-managed keys, that is a Private/Dedicated feature — we can include that option in the annex as an upgrade path.

Monica Patel

Subject: Re: US privacy annex — telemetry routing & emergency subprocessor onboarding

Laura / team — technical context from security:

- Dataflow: our hosted telemetry pipeline ingests logs and metrics into a staging tier where we apply normalization, masking, and coarse-grain hashing for identifiers. Raw PII is not stored persistently; raw traces are truncated and rotated into a short-lived buffer (default 48 hours). See attached dataflow diagram.
- Pseudonymization: we can apply one-way hashing with salt prior to export. Note: hashing across systems may reduce investigatory value; where customers require incident-level debugging we can provide ephemeral access under strict controls.
- Encryption & KMS: encryption at rest is always enabled. Customer-managed KMS (bringing your own key) is supported only in Redwood Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers we can offer envelope encryption and the option to rotate salts on demand.
- Onshore fallback: if HealthCo requires logs to remain onshore, we can route Covered Telemetry to a US-only cluster; this is subject to capacity planning and may require Dedicated capacity for guaranteed SLOs.

I recommend the contract include: (a) operative definition of Covered Telemetry, (b) the 72-hour notice SLA, (c) a requirement that emergency subprocessors accept pseudonymization as a default, and (d) an availability statement describing the onshore fallback option and expected procurement timeline for Dedicated capacity.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the diagram.

Rafael Mendes
Security & Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference

Dylan / Monica / Rafael — thanks for the quick turn. Procurement reviewed the redline and security notes; overall this looks workable for HealthCo, pending a couple of final items: 

1) Please provide the tracked redline as a single PDF (we received it but procurement wants an executive "one-pager" summary with the legal change highlights).
2) We need a clear SLA statement for the 72-hour notice (can it be "best effort with escalation to account exec" or must it be "contractual 72-hour SLA with remedy?"). Procurement prefers contractual SLA language; legal will escalate to pricing if there is a remedy.

If you can send the exec summary and confirm SLA language by COB Monday we can proceed to signature and attach the procurement checklist (attached). Also note we will require HIPAA scoping language if HealthCo's workloads include ePHI — can you confirm whether your hosted offering remains an option there, or whether we must plan for Private/Dedicated?
